source.title: SAEmnesia: Erasing Concepts in Diffusion Models with Supervised Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: E. Cassano; Riccardo Renzulli; Marco Nurisso; Mirko Zaffaroni; A. Perotti; Marco Grangetto

record.tranche_reason: The study reports evidence that unsupervised SAE features can be distributed or overlapping, tests supervised training intended to centralize concepts in individual latents, and reports cases where this centralization is incomplete or does not eliminate interference.
record.gate_note: The paper directly measures concept-to-latent score distributions, single-latent classification, and Cats–Dogs overlap, and reports single- versus two-latent nudity erasure results. General unlearning, attack robustness, and image-quality results are not rows because they do not measure whether SAE features are complete, canonical units. Hyperparameter-search counts and settings are not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: Most of the paper reports the performance of its own supervised SAE, which is trained on purpose to put each concept in one latent. Those rows do not test V5. The unsupervised SAE (SAeUron) measurements do bear on V5. On SD v1.5 cross-attention activations they show labelled concepts spread across many low-scoring latents. They also show the top latent is spatially incomplete and temporally inconsistent, and that Cats and Dogs share a most-active latent. These results qualify the claim that dictionary features are complete, canonical units.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that unsupervised SAEs split concepts across many latents. They report that supervised concept-assignment training centralizes each concept in one latent, giving better and cheaper erasure than SAeUron on UnlearnCanvas, in sequential unlearning, under attacks, and on I2P nudity (where two latents are used). They acknowledge within-group interference between similar concepts and limited scalability to very large vocabularies.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains supervised sparse autoencoders on diffusion-model activations and measures concept-to-latent mappings; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across SAE training variants and between from-scratch and finetuned training. Similar concepts can still interfere. Nudity erasure differs between one- and two-latent steering.

fits_no_version.finding: A supervised loss can force one-to-one concept–latent mappings: a dominant score peak forms, and the top latent matches all-latent k-NN accuracy. How much Cats/Dogs overlap remains varies widely across training variants (0 to 14 timesteps).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which SAE latents carry a concept depends on the training objective. Concept-to-latent structure is malleable, which bears on whether dictionary features are canonical.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The centralization evidence is from a limited diffusion-model setting and labeled concepts; stability across runs is not established. Some centralization evidence is figure-based without exact plotted values. The Cats–Dogs overlap results vary across SAE variants, and the nudity experiment reports that one latent performs weakly.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. The unlearning benchmark, sequential-unlearning, attack-robustness, and image-quality outcomes were not included because they do not directly measure feature centralization or whether SAE features are canonical units.

untested.parts: Stability of features across seeds or runs. Completeness of reconstruction. Canonicity across dictionary sizes. Any LLM setting. Only labelled object concepts in one SD v1.5 block are examined.
Not addressed; no LLMs are studied.

missing.what: Additional score histograms for SAeUron versus SAEmnesia on Architectures, Rabbits and Sea. Unsupervised max scores are 0.0054, 0.0117 and 0.0206, and the text calls them dispersed. The mapping of values to panels is ambiguous in the extracted text.
An unsupervised SAE on SDXL Turbo barely exceeds the no-unlearning baseline (Avg 49.73 vs 50.00). This is weak indirect evidence on how usable unsupervised concept latents are.

record.verdict_notes: Only the unsupervised-SAE comparator results bear on V5. All rows on SAEmnesia variants describe deliberately induced centralization and are relinked to none. The evidence on unsupervised SAEs is mostly figures with textual description, not quantitative splitting measures. Feature splitting of human-labelled concepts limits V5's 'complete units' reading but does not refute features being the model's units at a finer grain.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse features exceeding dimensions, near-orthogonal geometry, and a sparsity-dependent transition are not tested.
The study does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
It does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons independent of capacity pressure.
The experiments are on diffusion models, not LLMs; they do not test feature distributions or SAE recovery in LLMs.

The study tests concept centralization and whether a selected latent can carry useful concept information in particular diffusion-model settings. It does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable across training runs or settings, or canonical units generally.
The study uses individual scalar SAE latents but does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features as the underlying units of superposition.

rows.subject: SAeUron
rows.operation_detail: Measured the feature-importance score distribution for the Flowers concept.
rows.measure: Maximum feature-importance score
rows.note: The text describes scores as relatively uniform and low-magnitude across the latent space, consistent with distributed representation.
rows.check: The state should be absent, not reversed. The unsupervised SAE shows no dominant concept latent: scores are uniform and low (max 0.0166), which the paper attributes to feature splitting.

rows.operation_detail: Measured the feature-importance score distribution after supervised SAE training.
rows.measure: Maximum feature-importance score
rows.note: The paper reports a dominant peak at neuron 11979 and says the maximum is 2.43 times the baseline.
rows.check: This is the study's own supervised method, trained explicitly to centralize concepts. Induced centralization says nothing about whether SAE features are canonical units.

relationships.condition: Unsupervised TopK SAE (SAeUron) on SD v1.5 up.1.1 cross-attention activations, UnlearnCanvas object concepts
relationships.reason: Concept scores are dispersed (max 0.0166) and the top latent is spatially and temporally incomplete (r1, r7, r8). Cats and Dogs share a most-active latent at 10 timesteps (r11, r17). Single unsupervised latents therefore do not correspond to complete concept units.
relationships.display_finding: Concept scores were dispersed (maximum 0.0166), the top latent covered each concept incompletely in space and time, and Cats and Dogs shared a most-active latent at 10 timesteps, so single latents were not complete concept units.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
